A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from convex hull feasibility to convex hull membership. Their complete text, equations, algorithms and appendices are readable, and v2's added figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms, theoretical bounds and proofs, including the Gaussian unknown-variance extension, but reports no original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: Section 7 reports original seven-arm Bernoulli simulations. Figures 1–2 show empirical stopping complexity and sampling allocations.

M1.justification: The displayed sampling-weight formulas in Theorems 2 and 4 drop v1's time averages of sampled extrema. The Gaussian unknown-variance adaptation is removed, and Algorithm 2 introduces categorical sampling with oracle allocation functions for higher dimensions. The core conditional-sampling structure is retained under the Thompson-CHM name.

E1.justification: V2 establishes empirical coverage absent from v1: seven Bernoulli arms with means 0.1 through 0.7, evaluated at thresholds inside and above their convex hull. Higher-dimensional and Pareto applications remain theoretical rather than experimentally evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither PDF empirically evaluates competing algorithms. V2's plots compare against theoretical lower bounds and oracle allocations; its comparison with two successive Murphy-sampling tests is analytical.

E3.justification: V2 introduces the first empirical protocol, using Beta priors, a specified stopping-threshold function, six feasible and five infeasible threshold values, stopping complexity normalized by log(1/delta), and per-arm sampling fractions. V1 has no corresponding experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a threshold-sensitivity sweep, and Figure 2 diagnoses allocation behavior against oracle weights at gamma = 0.25 and 0.9. These are focused analyses of one fixed bandit configuration.

E5.justification: Figure 2 newly reports that allocation estimates use 100 repetitions. V1 contains no empirical run reporting. V2 supplies no seeds, uncertainty intervals or error bars for these estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 add original stopping-complexity and allocation results absent from v1. Empirical complexity exceeds the theoretical lower bound; infeasible-case allocations closely match oracle weights, while feasible-case allocations show visible gaps. These are newly reported results, not cross-version performance improvements.

T1.justification: V1's Gaussian Theorems 5–7, Lemma 6.2 and associated proofs are removed. V2 adds an extreme-point definition, a higher-dimensional characteristic-time/allocation theorem and arguments in Sections 9.2.1–9.2.2. The main one-dimensional bounds and proofs are largely retained, with revised sampling-weight conditions in Theorems 2 and 4.

C1.justification: V2 drops the advertised unknown-variance optimality contribution and adds higher-dimensional structural results, a potential algorithmic extension and empirical agreement at realistic time horizons. The central one-dimensional lower-bound and asymptotic-optimality claims remain.

C2.justification: V1's interpretation of the sample-complexity cost of unknown variances is removed. V2 explains why two successive one-sided tests allocate samples inefficiently, develops a geometric projection argument, and explicitly leaves the oracle functions' exact forms and full higher-dimensional optimality unresolved.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly specifies an explicit stopping-threshold function and a Beta-prior choice for simulation, beyond v1's general asymptotic threshold conditions. The numerical confidence level and Beta shape parameters are unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Filippozzi et al. on deterministic CHM, Lin et al. on Pareto multi-task learning and Martinez et al. on minimax fairness. References to Jourdan et al., Kalantari and Katz-Samuels/Scott are removed. The central positioning around Murphy sampling and top-two Thompson sampling is retained.

P1.justification: The title and terminology shift from CHF to CHM, parts of the abstract and introduction are rewritten, and the conclusion moves ahead of the appendix. Much retained method and proof prose remains closely matched, with some old CHF headings and a stale Gaussian-extension reference surviving.

P2.justification: V2 adds two figures containing four plots and a second algorithm display. Algorithm 1's basic presentation and the single-column layout remain, while several displayed formulas are compressed into inline statements and surrounding text reflows.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful empirical visibility and develops the higher-dimensional discussion, but exchanges the substantial unknown-variance analysis for an oracle-dependent extension whose full optimality remains open. The numerical agreement claim is also qualified by sizable feasible-case gaps in Figures 1–2 and missing confidence-level/prior settings. These benefits and limitations do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
